response_priorities.action: Maintain plume-injection monitoring and aviation/air-quality coordination
response_priorities.rationale: The plume-injection and fire-weather terms are both high, and the narrative confirms pyrocumulonimbus smoke reaching the stratosphere.

response_priorities.action: Pre-position smoke-health support for sensitive facilities in the AOI
response_priorities.rationale: The local response-load index combines high smoke potential with dense school and medical-site exposure in the bounded AOI slice.

response_priorities.action: Expand clean-air shelter options before a severe recurrence
response_priorities.rationale: Only a small shelter count is present relative to the population proxy, leaving a large shelter-gap normalization.

mechanism_chain: Hot, very dry source weather and nonzero wind support intense fire behavior and smoke transport.
Positive dNBR and annual embedding change indicate a burned and disturbed source landscape.
Multiple pyrocumulonimbus firestorms lofted smoke to 15-19 km, high enough for stratospheric injection.
The local exposure proxy shows millions of people and many sensitive sites in the AOI, so smoke response capacity matters even where the AOI is only a proxy slice.
primary_gt.final_interpretation: The event is best treated as a high-potential pyroconvective smoke-injection episode with substantial local response-load implications; the severe recurrence scenario raises plume potential by about 4.406 points and response load by about 1.542 points.

event.event_name: 2019-2020 Australian smoke over the South Pacific
event.region_focus: Southeastern Australia and South Pacific smoke plume

judge_anchors: The answer should cite package-relative paths instead of external URLs.
The core baseline index is pyroconvective_smoke_potential near 79.623.
The local response-load index is near 76.147.
The severe recurrence scenario increases the plume potential to about 84.029 and response load to about 77.689.
The interpretation should connect fire weather, dNBR, pyrocumulonimbus injection, stratospheric smoke, and local exposure.
common_errors: Using outside web sources instead of package files
Treating the AOI exposure proxy as a continent-wide impact total
Using off-event point-weather winds instead of the ERA5-Land gridded mean wind vector
Using a single precipitation product instead of the required three-product consensus

criteria.name: Self-directed package discovery and citations
criteria.description: Identifies and cites package-relative paths across reports, weather, burn/remote-sensing, exposure, and geospatial evidence without relying on outside sources.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points if most evidence families are cited but one family is missing or paths are incomplete.

criteria.name: Event window and plume-context extraction
criteria.description: Uses the inclusive 2019-12-29 to 2020-01-10 window, firestorm lower bound 20, smoke altitude 15-19 km, stratospheric link, and firestorm rate near 1.538 per day.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for correct dates with incomplete plume-context extraction.

criteria.name: Source-weather computation
criteria.description: Computes maximum 2 m temperature near 39.040 C, precipitation consensus near 0.172 mm, ERA5 mean wind speed near 0.696 m/s, and the heat, dryness, wind, and fire-weather normalizations.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for using the right datasets but missing one conversion, consensus, or normalization.

criteria.name: Burn, remote-change, and plume-injection model
criteria.description: Computes dNBR and AlphaEarth disturbance normalizations, altitude midpoint 17.000 km, plume-injection normalization near 0.865, and baseline pyroconvective smoke potential near 79.623.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 2-3 points for correct formulas with small numeric mistakes; award 1 point for qualitative synthesis without the required indices.

criteria.name: Exposure and response-load model
criteria.description: Computes approximate AOI area near 76788.287 km2, population density near 46.808 per km2, OSM amenity counts, shelter gap near 0.722, and local response-load index near 76.147.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points if exposure data are used but the area, amenity counts, or shelter metric is incomplete.

criteria.name: Severe recurrence scenario
criteria.description: Applies the specified hotter, windier, drier, higher-burn, and higher-plume perturbations and reports scenario indices near 84.029 and 77.689 with deltas near 4.406 and 1.542.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1 point for applying only part of the scenario correctly.

criteria.name: Mechanism interpretation and response priorities
criteria.description: Provides exactly three ranked response actions with numeric priority scores and a concise mechanism chain tying fire weather, dNBR, pyroCb injection, stratospheric smoke, and local exposure together.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1 point for plausible but generic priorities that only partly use the computed results.
